main_text.p: quippe persequutor, cùm ad purgan dū ventrem speluncam fuisset ingressus, illic cum viris suis Dauid inerat, qui iam tam longo tempore persecutionis eius mala tolerabat. Cùmque cum viri sui ad feriendum Saul accenderent, fregit eos responsionibus, quia manum mittere in Christū Domini non deberet. Qui tamen occultè surrexit & oră chlamydis eius abscidit. Quid enim p Saul nisi mali Rectores, quid per Dauid nisi boni subditi designantur? Saul igitur ventrē purgare, est prauos Præpositos concep-tam in corde malitiā vsq; ad opera miseri odoris extendere, & cogita apud se noxia factis exterioribus exequendo monstrare. Quē tamē Dauid ferire metuit, quia piæ subditorū mentes, ab omni se peste obtrectationis abstinētes, præpositoř vitā nullo linguę gladio ꝑcutiāt etiam cùm de imperfectione reprehendunt. Qui & si quandò pro infirmitate sese abstinere vix possunt, vt extrema ꝗdam atq; ꝑpositorum mala, sed tamen humiliter loquantur, quasi oram chla-mydis silenter incidunt. page.notes: Doubtful readings: "p" before "Saul" (possibly a contraction or abbreviation mark) is copied as printed; "platę" (the ę may be a contraction) and "ꝑpositorum" / "ꝑcutiāt" (p with stroke) are read from the scan. The right-hand narrow column is empty. The left strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is excluded. Italic and roman use of "Dauid" varies in the scan and is marked here as the most likely reading.
